question: What is the primary purpose of essential drugs according to the World Health Organization?

options.A: To satisfy the priority healthcare needs of the majority of the population
options.B: To provide expensive alternatives for chronic illnesses
options.C: To replace all traditional remedies in rural communities
options.D: To ensure pharmaceutical companies maximize their global profits

explanation: Essential drugs are specifically selected to satisfy the priority healthcare needs of the majority of the population based on public health relevance. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is the concept of essential drugs particularly important for nurses practicing in Nigeria?

options.A: It allows nurses to manufacture medications locally
options.B: It helps nurses advocate for rational drug use and manage inventories in resource-constrained settings
options.C: It exempts nurses from prescribing any medications
options.D: It guarantees that nurses receive higher salaries

explanation: Understanding essential drugs enables nursing students and practitioners to manage pharmaceutical supplies effectively and promote rational drug use in limited-resource environments. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h1)

question: In what decade did the global movement and realization regarding essential drugs primarily take shape?
explanation: The essential drugs concept emerged in the 1970s when the WHO addressed the widespread lack of access to basic medicines in developing nations. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h2)

question: When did the World Health Organization publish its very first Model List of Essential Drugs?
explanation: The WHO published the first Model List of Essential Drugs in 1977, containing around 200 active substances for basic healthcare needs. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h2)

question: How often is the WHO Model List of Essential Drugs typically updated?
explanation: The WHO updates its Model List of Essential Drugs biennially through an evidence-based review process conducted by expert committees. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following is a primary criterion for selecting an essential drug?

options.A: High market price and luxury branding
options.B: Public health relevance and proven efficacy
options.C: Exclusive manufacturing by a single private company
options.D: Complex chemical structure requiring advanced laboratory synthesis

explanation: Essential drugs are selected based on public health relevance, scientific evidence of efficacy and safety, and comparative cost-effectiveness. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h3)

question: How does the essential drugs concept primarily affect patient out-of-pocket expenditures?

options.A: It increases costs by introducing rare imported medications
options.B: It reduces costs through standardized lists and bulk purchasing affordability
options.C: It eliminates all healthcare costs entirely through private insurance
options.D: It has no impact on the financial burden of patients

explanation: Standardization and bulk purchasing drive down unit costs, making treatments more affordable and reducing out-of-pocket expenses for patients. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is a clinical advantage of utilizing a restricted list of essential medicines?

options.A: It causes confusion among healthcare workers due to frequent drug changes
options.B: It enhances provider familiarity, leading to safer administration and fewer errors
options.C: It forces nurses to prescribe experimental therapies
options.D: It eliminates the need for patient monitoring

explanation: A restricted, well-known list of drugs improves provider familiarity, which supports safer administration and adherence to treatment guidelines. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is a major limitation of standard essential drug lists regarding regional health needs?

options.A: They always include too many expensive experimental drugs
options.B: They may fail to account for regional epidemiological variations or rare diseases
options.C: They automatically eliminate all infectious disease medications
options.D: They prevent any form of public healthcare delivery

explanation: Standard lists can sometimes overlook regional disease variations or rare conditions that require specialized therapeutics not featured on the national model list. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h5)

question: How can patient misconceptions undermine the success of essential drug programs?

options.A: Patients often equate higher cost with superior quality, resisting generic essential drugs
options.B: Patients refuse to take any medications administered by nurses
options.C: Patients insist on manufacturing their own herbal supplements exclusively
options.D: Patients demand that all drugs be administered intravenously

explanation: Perceptions that expensive medications are better can lead to resistance against using affordable, high-quality generic essential drugs. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which Nigerian regulatory agency works alongside the National Drug Policy to enforce drug safety and combat fake medications?
explanation: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) is responsible for regulating and enforcing drug safety within the Nigerian framework. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is one of the primary aims of integrating the essential drugs concept into Nigeria's National Drug Policy?

options.A: To promote the import of expensive luxury brand medications
options.B: To ensure accessibility of safe, efficacious, and affordable medicines for all citizens
options.C: To eliminate the nursing profession's involvement in medication administration
options.D: To replace all orthodox medicine with international herbal products

explanation: The NDP integrates essential drugs to guarantee that safe, effective, and affordable medicines are accessible to every citizen across the country. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h6)
